mechanisms.name: Associative / content-addressable retrieval
mechanisms.definition: Recalling a stored item from a partial or noisy cue via similarity or associative attention rather than exact keys.

mechanisms.name: Component ablation of composite systems
mechanisms.definition: Removing or replacing parts of a composite (LLM + adapters) system to test whether each part contributes.

mechanisms.name: Concept / sentence-level representation units
mechanisms.definition: Modelling units larger than tokens (concepts, patches, sentences, latent codes) as the primary prediction target or representation.

mechanisms.name: Memory consolidation and replay
mechanisms.definition: Transferring fast episodic memories into slow durable weights via replay, distillation or sleep-like phases.

mechanisms.name: Context compression
mechanisms.definition: Shrinking long context into fewer tokens, vectors or KV entries while preserving task information.

mechanisms.name: Continual plasticity
mechanisms.definition: Updating parameters or state after deployment without a separate training phase and without catastrophic forgetting.

mechanisms.name: Data-efficient pretraining
mechanisms.definition: Getting more from little data: repetition, synthetic rephrasing, curricula, multilingual sampling, schedules.

mechanisms.name: Error monitoring and verification
mechanisms.definition: Internal or auxiliary signals that predict an incorrect output or trajectory, with calibrated false-positive control.

mechanisms.name: Recurrent / fast-weight memory
mechanisms.definition: State updated within a sequence by a learning rule (delta rule, linear attention, SSM) acting as memory.

mechanisms.name: Fuzzy / compressed persistent memory
mechanisms.definition: Storing past experience in a compressed, lossy, persistent neural state (slots, soft KV, memory tokens) that is read without retrieving raw text.

mechanisms.name: Hierarchical planning
mechanisms.definition: Producing a coarse plan or abstract structure before filling in details.

mechanisms.name: Knowledge conflict / override
mechanisms.definition: How injected information competes with parametric priors and when it fails to override them.

mechanisms.name: Latent / continuous reasoning
mechanisms.definition: Performing intermediate reasoning in hidden states or recurrent depth instead of emitted tokens.

mechanisms.name: Learned neural communication between models
mechanisms.definition: Passing information between separately trained networks through learned vectors, stitching layers or latent channels instead of text.

mechanisms.name: Low-precision training effects
mechanisms.definition: Effects of BF16/FP8/INT optimizer states or weights on training quality.

mechanisms.name: Local / biologically plausible learning rules
mechanisms.definition: Learning without global backprop: Hebbian, local, forward-only, zeroth-order or spiking plasticity.

mechanisms.name: Non-autoregressive / coarse-to-fine generation
mechanisms.definition: Generating text other than strictly one token at a time left-to-right: parallel, iterative refinement, diffusion, multi-token, or coarse-to-fine code levels.

mechanisms.name: Representation convergence / alignment
mechanisms.definition: Evidence about whether independently trained networks learn compatible internal representations.

mechanisms.name: Mixture / specialist routing
mechanisms.definition: Selecting or composing among specialised experts, adapters or modules per input.

mechanisms.name: Test-time compute and search
mechanisms.definition: Spending more inference compute via sampling, search, or verification to improve answers.

mechanisms.name: Test-time training / optimization
mechanisms.definition: Optimizing parameters or memory on the test input at inference time.

mechanisms.name: Weight-space adaptation (hypernetworks, adapters)
mechanisms.definition: Writing information into parameters directly: generated LoRA, hypernetworks, weight editing, model merging.

mechanisms.name: World-state representation
mechanisms.definition: Maintaining an internal predictive model of environment or task state across time.
